title: What AI tools and models are you using for game development?
author: OperationLow1494
selftext:
Curious what everyone is using in their AI game dev pipelines.

I'm currently using Hermes with GPT-OSS 20B through Ollama on a 5070 Ti trying to get away from paid subs , and considering a 128GB Mac Studio to run larger models locally.

Mainly interested in coding agents, multi-agent setups, image generation, and automating development tasks.

What's everyone running? Any particular models, tools, or setups you'd recommend? What's actually working well for you?

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body: Mainly Claude. But I use chatgpt to polish the game system texts. Eleven labs for sound effects, and there's a website name Hailuo where I subscribed and generate sprites/images

comments.author: donkeykong917
comments.body:
I wouldn't use local models as they haven't been that great for building games in my experience. How much you planning to spend on a Mac studio versus how much it costs for a subscription. 

You could be paying less for the subscription and release the game than to invest in hardware. If you make the money then you could consider buy hardware.

comments.author: lorendroll
comments.body:
I strive to find the most economical and practical option for coding, so I use DeepSeek V4.1 Flash from deeprelay for $5 and free GLM 5.3 Flash from ZCode daily giveaways. This gives me the ability to use agents without regard to limits throughout the week, racing 12 hours a day. I also use Muse Spark 1.3 contributor via the API through OpenRouter for next to nothing and it is on par with them. I'm considering adding the cheapest Claude plan to run Sonnet or Opus as an orchestrator to improve quality and resolve complex issues, but I have expertise myself, so I do not see much use for it.

I also tried local Qwen and it is cool, but local models are too impractical, in my opinion, and the best you can run is a quantized DeepSeek which costs pennies from cloud providers in full precision.

Regarding 3D and image generators, I've heard that you can teach your local model to work via Higgsfield's API without having to manually intervene. I haven't tried it yet.

comments.author: Designisty
comments.body:
Codex (GPT 6.1 Sol) High / Extra High  
Deepseek 4.1 Flash for smaller coding tasks  
GTP Images 2 - Textures / Concept Art  
Suno - Music  
Elevan Labs - Voice / SFX  
3D AI Studio - 3D Models  
Blender (MCP) - 3D Modeling  
Godot (MCP) - Game Engine Contol   
Cascadeur - Animations  
Google Flow / Minimax H3 / LTX - Video Production

replies.author: OperationLow1494
replies.body: what do you use as a controller? aka master agent?

replies.author: Designisty
replies.body: Most things run through the Codex App :) 6.1 Sol

comments.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
comments.body:
Your setup is going to ensure your game doesn’t become great. All you need nowadays is Claude with blender, maybe ChatGPT to generate reference images for your game and you’re good to go. 

I’ve tried making games with weaker models, and they never turn out good

replies.author: OperationLow1494
replies.body: I use claude and chatgpt too lol, just messing with local models alongside them. it’s a pretty simple game design anyway, the hard part is making the survival loop fun and getting everything to work together.

replies.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
replies.body:
Right, we all think AI game development is just about giving your AI one prompt and stepping away until it’s done but it’s really a lot of work man.

I started an RPG game last week and completed the first map. Only need to realize that if I attempt to finish this game, it’s gonna take me probably six months of work. And sadly when I put it out, people are gonna complain that I made it with AI.

So now I’m wondering if I should finish the game or start a simple one that I can finish within a month.

replies.author: OperationLow1494
replies.body: well thats kinda where im at.... i have a idea that I think will be pretty popular but I'm having a hard time getting the LOOK right. But I say screw em if it is or isn't so long as its fun playable supported an ai game shouldn't really matter.

replies.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
replies.body:
I think you’re onto something. Personally if a game is fun , I wouldn’t care if it was made with AI or not. 

But at the same time, I understand why people don’t like it because I don’t want to listen to AI music or watch AI movies no matter how good they are. 

But anyway have you thought about paying for pre built assets?

comments.author: CrimsonBolt33
comments.body:
GPT-OSS 20B

thats horrible...thats such an old model...

  
you need to look into [Strata](https://github.com/niko1221/strata)...it can run a much better much more recent model (Qwen 3.8 next flash) at proper speeds.

  
Also the price for a mac to run local models only works if you have something running locally 24/7 more or less. Otherwise a subscription or two makes more sense.

comments.author: Upbeat-Mail7201
comments.body: Mainly Claude Opus 5.5 on Extra High and High depending on the task, as well as ChatGPT for conception, Gemini for sketches and interactive mind maps, documentation and brainstorming, I sometimes also built super small python or html/JS prototypes of a specific mechanic we want to implement and test the idea beforehand, but also Elevenlabs, autosprite and several stock libraries, a real sound designer, real graphic designers and ofc a real game designer no local models they are too slow and we only have shitty MacBooks from 2021 haha
